nodes.content: Learn insertion policies from demonstrations that transfer across robot embodiments and unseen object compliance while respecting contact-force limits.
requirements: Achieve 80% success on unseen embodiment–compliance pairs, exceeding same-data behavior cloning by 15 percentage points.
Keep peak contact force below object-specific damage thresholds in at least 95% of trials.

nodes.content: Train an object-frame diffusion policy on demonstrations with robot-specific impedance adapters, online compliance inference, and object-specific force-threshold shielding.
Can online compliance inference distinguish soft from rigid sockets using force-limited contact trajectories across unseen robot arms?
Damage-threshold-capped micro-probes classify unseen soft versus rigid sockets with ≥90% accuracy across held-out arms and ≥95% force-safe trials.
Run 200 object-threshold-capped micro-probes on held-out arms with unseen soft and rigid sockets; record classification accuracy and force violations.
Across 200 held-out-arm probes, soft/rigid classification reached 92% (184/200), and 97% (194/200) stayed below object-specific damage thresholds.
Adopt threshold-capped micro-probes for compliance inference: held-out-arm classification reached 92%, with 97% of probes below damage thresholds.
Integrate adopted micro-probes; evaluate insertion success and damage-threshold violations against same-data behavior cloning on unseen arm–compliance pairs.
Run 400 InsertShift trials on unseen arm–compliance pairs, comparing probe-conditioned diffusion versus same-data behavior cloning on success and damage-threshold exceedance.
InsertShift v1 evaluation bundle containing 400 trial logs, arm–compliance splits, success labels, peak-force traces, and behavior-cloning comparisons.
Audit InsertShift v1 logs for complete force traces, then bootstrap paired success gains and threshold-safe rates by arm–compliance split.
InsertShift v1: probe-conditioned diffusion succeeded in 162/200 trials (81%) versus cloning's 130/200 (65%); 192/200 (96%) avoided damage-threshold violations.
Run InsertShift v1 ablations disabling object-frame normalization, impedance adapters, compliance probing, or force shielding; compare success and force safety.
On 40 unseen highly compliant sockets, the full policy succeeded 23/40 versus 30/40 without probing; 6/40 breached damage thresholds.
Retain the policy for other tested pairs, but withhold highly compliant deployment pending probe redesign and force-safety validation.
Refine adopted micro-probes into compliance-adaptive, lower-amplitude probes; retest highly compliant pairs for ≥80% success, ≥15-point cloning gain, ≥95% threshold safety.
Use InsertShift v1 force traces to fit a compliance-adaptive probe controller capped at 25% of each socket’s damage threshold.
InsertShift v2 bundle retains v1 logs and adds the fitted compliance-adaptive probe controller, 25%-threshold caps, and revised evaluation protocol.
Distill demonstrations into a morphology-conditioned contact-state policy with passive compliance inference and damage-threshold-constrained model-predictive control, avoiding micro-probes.
Can passive contact-state histories identify unseen socket compliance quickly enough for force-constrained insertion without deliberate probing?
Passive force–pose histories identify unseen compliance within 0.4 seconds at ≥85% accuracy, enabling ≥95% threshold-safe insertions without probes.
Replay 240 held-out-arm insertions with passive force–pose estimation; score compliance accuracy at 0.4 seconds and object-threshold-safe trial rate.
On 240 held-out-arm insertions, 0.4-second passive compliance accuracy was 79% (190/240); 96% (230/240) stayed threshold-safe.
Run 200 unseen arm–compliance insertions with passive inference and constrained control; measure success, threshold safety, and compliance identification latency.
On 200 unseen-pair insertions, 0.4-second passive compliance accuracy reached 87% (174/200), success 81% (162/200), and threshold safety 97% (194/200).
Conditionally advance passive control: both tests exceeded 95% force safety, but repeat compliance inference because 0.4-second accuracy varied 79%–87%.
Stratify cohorts by arm and compliance; recalibrate passive uncertainty; retest 0.4-second accuracy, insertion success, and threshold safety.
Collect 320 fresh insertion trials balanced across four unseen arms and four compliance bins; log 0.4-second predictions and peak forces.
PassiveInsert-Balanced v1: 320 fresh trials, 20 per arm–compliance bin, with timestamped compliance predictions, success labels, and peak-force traces.
Train a demonstration-seeded contact-mode skill graph with compliance-randomized simulation and embodiment-invariant wrench control under damage-threshold barrier constraints.
Can randomized contact-mode skills transfer across unseen arms and socket compliance without losing force safety at mode transitions?
Contact-mode skills achieve ≥80% unseen-pair success, beat cloning by ≥15 points, and keep ≥95% transition trials threshold-safe.
Use PassiveInsert-Balanced v1 to stratify 320 new held-out-pair trials comparing skill-graph and same-data cloning success and transition-force safety.
Skill-graph success was 80% (128/160) versus cloning’s 64% (102/160), but only 93% (149/160) of transition trials stayed threshold-safe.
Predictive wrench-budget guards at contact-mode transitions raise threshold-safe trials to ≥95% while preserving ≥80% success and ≥15-point cloning gain.
Run 320 PassiveInsert-Balanced v1-stratified trials comparing guarded versus unguarded skill graphs on success, cloning gain, and transition-force safety.
Unguarded: 130/160 successes versus cloning’s 102/160, with 154/160 threshold-safe transitions; guarded: 122/160 successes despite 157/160 threshold-safe transitions.
Tune guard hysteresis from n37 failures; run 320 PassiveInsert-Balanced v1-stratified trials versus unguarded skills and cloning, measuring success and threshold-safety.
Unguarded: 132/160 successes, 155/160 threshold-safe versus cloning’s 102/160 successes; hysteresis-guarded: 126/160 successes, 158/160 threshold-safe.
Advance unguarded skills for independent safety validation; guards reduced success below 80%, while unguarded threshold safety varied 93%–97%.
Run 400 independent held-out arm–compliance trials, comparing unguarded skills with cloning and stratifying success and transition-force violations.
Stratify 400 independent trials using transition-failure profiles from n34, n37, and n39; compare unguarded skills with cloning.
SkillTransfer-400 v1 contains independent arm–compliance splits, skill-graph/cloning trial logs, transition peak-force traces, success labels, and damage thresholds.
Retarget demonstrated insertion trajectories through differentiable contact models, optimizing against uncertain compliance with conformal peak-force constraints.
Do conformal peak-force bounds remain calibrated when contact-model retargeting encounters unseen arm–compliance pairs?
Compliance-stratified conformal bounds cover ≥95% of peak-force errors on unseen arm–compliance pairs, yielding ≥95% damage-threshold-safe insertions.
Retarget demonstrations using InsertShift v2 calibration traces; test conformal force coverage, insertion success, and threshold safety across 200 unseen pairs.
On 200 unseen pairs, conformal coverage reached 96% (192/200); retargeting succeeded 82% versus cloning’s 65%, with 97% threshold-safe.
Using InsertShift v2 calibration, stress-test retargeting on 80 unseen highly compliant sockets; record conformal coverage, success, and damage-threshold violations.
On 80 highly compliant sockets, retargeting succeeded 59/80 (74%); conformal coverage was 68/80 (85%), with 9/80 damage-threshold violations.
Advance broader validation after 82% success and 97% safety; exclude highly compliant sockets given 85% coverage and 89% safety.
Keep highly compliant sockets deployment-excluded; recalibrate bounds and independently test ≥95% coverage and force safety on unseen pairs.
Recalibrate compliance-stratified bounds using n48/n50 residuals; run 240 fresh unseen-pair trials, including excluded sockets only in supervised tests.
ConformalRetarget-240 v1 contains recalibrated bounds and 240 supervised trial logs, stratified coverage, success labels, peak forces, and exclusions.
Learn embodiment-invariant wrench–pose successor features from demonstrations; train conservative offline RL with object-specific damage-budget action filtering.
Can demonstration-derived wrench–pose successor features generalize across unseen arms and socket compliance while supporting damage-budget filtering?
Successor-feature offline RL yields ≥80% unseen-pair success, ≥15-point cloning gain, and ≥95% damage-threshold safety with action filtering.
Train successor-feature RL on SkillTransfer-400; calibrate filters with ConformalRetarget-240; test success and force safety against cloning on 200 fresh pairs.
On 200 fresh pairs, successor-feature RL succeeded 164/200 (82%) versus cloning’s 130/200 (65%); 192/200 (96%) stayed damage-threshold-safe.
Train on SkillTransfer-400, calibrate filters on ConformalRetarget-240; test 120 unseen highly compliant pairs for success, cloning gain, and force safety.
On 120 unseen highly compliant pairs, RL succeeded 86/120 (72%) versus cloning’s 70/120 (58%); 110/120 (92%) remained damage-threshold-safe.
Compliance-conditioned successor features and uncertainty-calibrated force filters achieve ≥80% success, ≥15-point cloning gain, and ≥95% safety on highly compliant pairs.
Train revised and original RL variants using SkillTransfer-400 and ConformalRetarget-240; compare 240 held-out highly compliant trials against cloning.
Across 80 highly compliant trials each, original RL: 65 successes, 77 safe; revised: 60 successes, 78 safe; cloning: 52 successes.
Using n64 failures and SkillTransfer-400/ConformalRetarget-240, test original/revised RL against cloning on success and safety across 360 highly compliant trials.
Across 120 highly compliant trials each, original RL: 98 successes, 115 safe; revised: 92 successes, 117 safe; cloning: 78 successes.
Conditionally select original RL over revision: later highly compliant cohorts met targets, but the earlier 120-trial cohort failed all three.
Prospectively retest original RL on independent, compliance-stratified unseen pairs; compare cloning success and damage-threshold safety, investigating earlier failures.
Stratify 400 fresh unseen-pair trials using n59/n61/n64/n66 failure patterns; compare original RL and cloning success and damage-threshold safety.
SuccessorTransfer-400 v1 logs 400 prospective trials with arm–compliance strata, original-RL/cloning assignments, insertion outcomes, peak forces, and damage thresholds.
